Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
307 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The Wind Advisory has been expanded to include our entire forecast 
area. 

Forecasted rainfall amounts have increased slightly across most of 
our area.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. A robust low pressure system is likely to impact the area
today and Thanksgiving Day. There is potential for frequent wind
gusts strong enough to bring down temporary outdoor structures
such as tents and holiday decorations, and produce isolated power
outages. Widespread rainfall is expected with locally heavy rain
possible, however the overall flood risk appears low.
2. Gusty winds redevelop Thursday afternoon and continue through
Friday with light wintry precipitation possible near the Tennessee
border. Warmer for the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: A robust low pressure system is likely to impact the 
area today and Thanksgiving Day. There is potential for frequent 
wind gusts strong enough to bring down temporary outdoor structures 
such as tents and holiday decorations, and produce isolated power 
outages. Widespread rainfall is expected with locally heavy rain 
possible, however the overall flood risk appears low.

Sprawling sfc high pressure centered to our north continues to  
produce gusty NE winds and relatively dry dewpts across our area. 
As the morning progresses, the high is expected to strengthen a bit 
more under confluent upper flow. This will result in a classical CAD 
set-up that will impact much of the East Coast including our CWA, 
thru at least Thursday morning. Cloud cover continues to increase 
from south to north overnight, however temps are still expected to 
fall into the mid to upper 30s over most of the Piedmont. A few 
locations near I-40 and in the mtn valleys nearer the Blue Ridge 
Escarpment could fall below freezing. Precipitation chances increase 
from south to north thru the day today, but it's still looking like 
precip doesn't begin until temperatures warm above freezing, and/or 
cloud cover keeps temps above freezing altogether. Temperatures remain 
steady or even warm later tonight and into Thursday as wedge erosion 
begins. Thus, no wintry precip appears possible during this period. 

Consensus is strengthening for a robust sfc low to develop over the
east coast of Florida later today and track northward. Moist ELY flow
over the damming sfc high results in widespread precip for our CWA by
this evening, continuing overnight before generally tapering off from 
SW to NE during the day on Thanksgiving. Overall, expected QPF amounts
remain similar to previous fcsts, but they have trended a bit higher 
over most of our NC Piedmont and foothill zones. We now have 1 to 2" 
storm total amounts fcst across a good portion of those areas. Still, 
few global model ensemble members develop enough QPF for much of a 
flood risk. It is possible that a narrow, frontogenetically-forced 
band of heavy rain could develop west of the low track, which models 
may not resolve well. Nonetheless, the flash flood threat still appears 
low and likely secondary to the threat posed by strong/gusty winds. 
WPC maintains a Marginal Risk for most of our fcst area on the Day 2 
Excessive Rainfall Outlook. 

As for the winds, we are still expecting anomalously strong easterly 
925 to 850mb winds associated with the LLJ, with winds of 45 to 50 kt 
possible a couple thousand feet above ground over the Piedmont. Given 
the strength of the wedge and the associated inversion, we still expect 
only shallow mixing and thus these higher gusts will likely be limited 
over the Piedmont. Nonetheless, there is good support among the latest 
model guidance for frequent 30 to 45 mph gusts from Wednesday afternoon 
thru Thursday morning. Peak winds for the event will likely be closer to 
45 mph for most locations with higher gusts expected at the higher ele-
vations (ie, above 3500 ft). After consultation with our neighboring 
fcst offices, we decided to expand the Wind Advisory to include our 
entire CWA. The valid time remains the same as the initial Advisory, 
noon today until 10 AM Thursday. This was largely done because of the
potential for significant impacts across our area. A few power outages 
could result and gusts will be capable of blowing over holiday decora-
tions, tents, portable canopies, etc, many of which are only rated for 
25 mph gusts. Be prepared for wind gusts to turn over outdoor cooking 
appliances; have a fire extinguisher handy.


Key message 2: Gusty winds redevelop Thursday afternoon and continue
through Friday with light wintry precipitation possible near the 
Tennessee border. Warmer for the weekend.

A noticeable lull in wind speed appears likely Thursday morning as 
low pressure pulls away to the north and before cold-air advection 
on its back side induces stronger mixing. Gusty winds are expected 
to return Thursday afternoon and continue thru Friday. We cannot 
completely rule out Advisory-level gusts over the higher mountain 
elevations, but the threat still appears lower compared to today
thru Thursday morning. Temperatures are expected to rebound to within 
a few degrees of normal for Thursday afternoon, but trend colder again 
Thursday night. Light NW-flow precipitation Thurs night may change to 
a wintry mix, if not snow or rime ice. It's looking like there should 
be sufficient moisture to maintain at least a solid-chance PoP along 
portions of the NC/TN border thru the day Friday. Any accumulations 
should be minimal. 

Temperatures trend warmer over the weekend. More of the latest long-
range guidance now has a fast-moving cold front push thru our area
late Sunday into early Monday with some amount of precip associated
with the fropa. If this scenario pans out, temperatures should be 
warm enough that only rain is possible.

&&

.AVIATION /08Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Dry and VFR through daybreak. Gusty winds 
have already developed across KCLT and the SC terminals this morning 
and will continue through the end of the TAF period. Gusts should 
develop by late morning at KHKY and late afternoon at KAVL, 
lingering through the end of the TAF period. Wind gusts will range 
from 20-30 kts through the morning hours, increasing to 25-35 kts 
this afternoon into tonight. OVC through the period with RA and 
restrictions spreading across the terminals between 13Z and 16Z. 
Went with a PROB30 for the onset of RA and restrictions as guidance 
is still not in great agreement regarding onset timing. Once RA 
starts, it will linger though late tonight so have prevailing RA 
once PROB30s end. Cigs should drop to MVFR mid to late morning and 
IFR by the afternoon. LIFR cigs may develop briefly at KCLT late 
this evening but confidence is too low to mention in the TAF at this 
time. Vsby restrictions will mostly be MVFR to IFR with the 
precipitation shield. 

Outlook: Widespread rain, gusty winds and associated restrictions 
will gradually wane Thursday as a strong low pressure system lifts 
away from the terminals. Drier and VFR conditions return Thursday 
night into Saturday but gusty winds will return Thursday afternoon 
and should linger into Friday evening.
